Khashchuvate New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kirovohrad Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Khashchuvate, known since 1362 as Kachuchinka under the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, saw its Jewish community reach 3,266 people (71 percent) by 1897, supporting two synagogues. The community endured pogroms in 1918 and 1920; by the 1930s, about 260 Jews worked on three Jewish kolkhozes, supported by a Jewish council and Yiddish school. All of Khashchuvate's Jewish population was murdered in February 1942, following the July 1941 German occupation. This new cemetery, established in the 1940s per both IAJGS and ESJF survey findings, remains in active use and well kept.
